content.rationale: The new verb: without --on (lptlmrtv) or without -m (N7) it refuses and creates nothing; an argument the form does not name refuses, named (N8), and the form's flags are recognized in any order (N9); when the --on set names anything that does not resolve it refuses before birth, naming each unknown id (D22, mtqypkwo, nmnlqoyx); otherwise it brackets the birth through M-markers-capture — the lifecycle table's creation case (S5-lifecycle) — opening the change after the named dependencies through M-jj-new (S3-new; the position is the newest dependency, its unique head in jj history, S3-new-position, and a --on set with more than one head refuses before anything is created, naming each tied id, S3-new-position refusal; placement is ylvpykys), taking the change id the crossing reports as the node's id (D12; file identity is oyxxypuz), and writing the skeleton N6 fixes through M-store-write's atomic replacement — never std::fs, never a truncate. A write that cannot be completed comes back as a value, which the verb turns into its refusal, naming the cause (S2-write-refusal-site, myoztqyu). A birth that cannot complete abandons the change it opened (S5-birth-fail, kvwonkzy) through M-jj-abandon (urtkpxwv) — the crossing reports no usable id, or the write fails — and only then refuses, carrying the abandon's own failure rather than swallowing it. The skeleton is kind decision (pzquqmrq), type text with ref inline and placeholder content (tvouykvz) and a placeholder rationale (swqoqoso), and it validates against the node schema the CLI carries (wrmumorm); its depends_on holds exactly the given ids (msyrpuol) and the change carries the summary (yuznnnlx). The created id is printed as one line (O6, pqxtmwqw). It resolves through M-node-resolve (whose root exception makes zzzzzzzz a placeable dependency), names the file through M-store-path, reads through M-store-read across the runner (M-jj) and writes through M-store-write, builds its refusals through M-refusal, takes the injected context (M-context, M-context-injection), and returns its lines for the envelope to write (M-output-return) under M-route's handler shape — the table's Verb type, which its signature must match — carrying its own --help text (xlvoxmyl/rwlywqrk, per oqnsuzqu) — answered before the store is taken, so a root-less context still answers it (H1, qtqnuqxo), as do the form's refusals. I1-serde fixes the JSON layer the document is written with. It takes the store through the context's fallible accessor for the operation, after the surface is answered (S3-root-required). The read's refusal site (S2-read-refusal-site, vollyzvn) is this invocation's: a --on target whose document cannot be read refuses before birth, naming it. A refused birth answers no target — the change it opened is abandoned (S5-birth-fail, kvwonkzy), so there is nothing to record — and no marker lands (S5-record-named, wotmvzyt); a born change records one creation marker naming the id it printed.
